fixture.name: 12 chronological small inserts, 2000 stable slots and 2000 rotating slots changing generation every 3 inserts

method: One matched stock O1 server; both physical TimeSeries tables share identical input bytes and hash generator, and differ only in inner ID type. 12 INSERTs/table with alternating order; after batches 4/8/12 explicit final MergeTree merges on TAGS/SAMPLES/TimeRanges per table. 24 QueryFinish and 18 MergeParts profile events present. Exact sample point parity checked by sum(length(samples)), not SAMPLES physical row count; native avg by(scope)(avg_over_time(metric[30m])) checked against independent Python mean oracle.
math_bound: Per part with N physical ID references and D distinct IDs, raw occupies ~16N bytes before codec; dictionary layout ~16D+wN plus hash/update overhead. Data codec and part boundaries determine actual bytes. This sample has 48000 sample points, 10000 distinct IDs per table; actual final SAMPLES physical rows 10000 due v11 bucketed arrays, so any naive 48000-row assertion is invalid.

correctness.precision: max observed between variants <1e-12, strict float tolerance 1e-8

merge_partlog.note: Three merges per target/variant; single run, no paired A/B/B/A; CPU totals descriptive only, not a causal speed claim

inserts.note: QueryFinish INSERT CPU events are ~15ms across 12 requests versus ~800ms total wall and omit substantial async storage work; do not claim meaningful write CPU improvement from this metric.

limitations: One run, 12 inserts and 3 explicit merges per table. Not continuous ingest with reads and natural background merges.
Storage size measured after full merges; no write amplification bytes over time or WAL measurement.
No matched fresh-server A/B/B/A or p95/p99; insertion CPU via query_log excludes async storage work.
Fixture uses only 10000 distinct IDs, deterministic stable/rotating distributions, not the larger 400-node/3h real workload. No production-specific jemalloc allocator control.
Native semantic oracle is for two grouped outcomes only, not NaN/late updates/ACL or regex.
stop_condition: Accept correctness and physical footprint as a baseline only; no production performance claim until process CPU seconds, read concurrency, background merge cost and drift are tested on repeated runs.

next_action.step: On the same pinned stock O1 binary and fixture, add process-level CPU and background-merge accounting to each of repeated same-runner A/B/B/A write phases, then monitor native query p95 while inserts continue; validate with an explicit no-write control.
next_action.stop_condition: Stop/promote only if exact sample/ID parity, disk/merge evidence and CPU accounting gates pass without OOM or baseline drift >25%.
